'''George Eyre Andrews''' (born December 4, 1938)<ref name="rlc"/> is an American [[mathematician]] working in [[special functions]], [[number theory]], [[mathematical analysis|analysis]] and [[combinatorics]].

==Education and career==
He is currently an Evan Pugh Professor of Mathematics at [[Pennsylvania State University]].<ref name="nas"/><ref>[http://www.research.psu.edu/about/faculty-staff-resources/faculty-honors-1/evan-pugh-professors Evan Pugh Professors] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203003230/http://www.research.psu.edu/about/faculty-staff-resources/faculty-honors-1/evan-pugh-professors |date=2013-12-03 }}, PSU, retrieved 2013-11-21.</ref> He did his undergraduate studies at [[Oregon State University]]<ref name="nas"/> and received his PhD in 1964 at the [[University of Pennsylvania]] where his advisor was [[Hans Rademacher]].<ref name="rlc"/><ref>{{MathGenealogy |id=7528}}</ref>

During 2008–2009 he was president of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/about-us/presidents/60-andrews AMS presidents, a timeline]</ref>

==Contributions==
Andrews's contributions include several monographs and over 250 research and popular articles on [[q-series]], [[special functions]], [[combinatorics]] and applications.<ref name="mactutor"/><ref>[http://www.emis.de/journals/SLC/wpapers/s42askey.pdf The work of George Andrews: a Madison perspective] – by [[Richard Askey]], in "The Andrews Festschrift (Maratea, 1998)", Sem. Lothar. Combin. vol. 42 (1999), Art. B42b, 24 pp.
</ref> He is considered to be the world's leading expert in the theory of [[integer partition]]s.<ref name="rlc">{{citation|title=Ramanujan: Letters and Commentary|volume=9|series=History of Mathematics|editor1-first=Bruce C.|editor1-last=Berndt|editor2-first=Robert Alexander|editor2-last=Rankin|publisher=American Mathematical Society|year=1995|isbn=9780821891254|page=305|bibcode=1995rlc..book.....B|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Of5G0r6DQiEC&pg=PA305|quote=Andrews is generally recognized as the world's leading authority on partitions and is the author of the foremost treatise on the subject.}}</ref><ref>{{citation|title=Ramanujan's Place in the World of Mathematics: Essays Providing a Comparative Study|first=Krishnaswami|last=Alladi|authorlink= Krishnaswami Alladi |publisher=Springer|year=2012|isbn=9788132207672|page=122|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=XLNJDylP53QC&pg=PA122|quote=George Andrews of the Pennsylvania State University, the world authority on partitions and ''q''-geometric series}}.</ref> In 1976 he discovered [[Ramanujan]]'s [[Ramanujan's lost notebook|Lost Notebook]].<ref name="nas"/> He is interested in mathematical pedagogy.<ref name="nas"/>

His book ''The Theory of Partitions'' is the standard reference on the subject of [[integer partition]]s.<ref name="rlc"/>

He has advanced mathematics in the theories of partitions and q-series. His work at the interface of number theory and combinatorics has also led to many important applications in physics.<ref name=UIllinois/>

==Awards and honors==
In 2003 Andrews was elected a member of the [[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="nas">[[Regina Nuzzo]] (2005) [http://www.pnas.org/cgi/content/full/102/13/4663 Biography of George E. Andrews] @ [[PNAS]]</ref> He was elected a Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1997.<ref name=AAAS>{{cite web|title=Book of Members, 1780-2010: Chapter A|url=http://www.amacad.org/publications/BookofMembers/ChapterA.pdf|publisher=American Academy of Arts and Sciences|access-date=18 April 2011}}</ref> In 1998 he was an Invited Speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Berlin.<ref>{{cite book|author=Andrew, George E.|chapter=Mathematics education: Reform or renewal?|title=Doc. Math. (Bielefeld) Extra Vol. ICM Berlin, 1998, vol. III|year=1998|pages=719–721|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011626000}}</ref> In 2012 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2012-11-03.</ref>

He was given honorary doctorates from the [[University of Parma]] in 1998, the [[University of Florida]] in 2002, the [[University of Waterloo]] in 2004, [[SASTRA University]] in [[Kumbakonam]], India in 2012, and [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]] in 2014.<ref name="mactutor">{{MacTutor Biography|id=Andrews}}</ref><ref>[http://lists.siam.org/pipermail/siam-opsf/2013-January/000077.html Honorary doctorates for Andrews, Askey and Berndt]</ref><ref name=UIllinois>{{cite web|title=University of Illinois commencement ceremony to take place May 17 at Memorial Stadium (honorary doctorates for George E. Andrews and Phillip Allen Sharp)|date=5 May 2014|website=Campus News (illinois.edu)|url=http://news.illinois.edu/news/14/0505commencement_2014.html}}</ref>
